sources.note: A training-free residual-stream steering method that mitigates overthinking by projecting a difference-in-means 'overthinking direction' onto a low-dimensional PCA manifold of the model's activations before ablating it, removing the accuracy-degrading interference noise that limits naive single-direction steering.
sources.title: Mitigating Overthinking in Large Reasoning Models via Manifold Steering

sources.note: A survey that organizes methods for making R1-style large reasoning models reason efficiently (i.e., avoid overthinking) into two axes: single-model optimization and multi-model collaboration.
sources.title: Don't Overthink It: A Survey of Efficient R1-style Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: ReBalance is a training-free inference-time steering method that reads a reasoning model's token confidence to detect overthinking or underthinking and applies a hidden-state steering vector to shorten or extend the chain of thought accordingly.
sources.title: Efficient Reasoning with Balanced Thinking

sources.note: Identifies that overthinking in large reasoning models corresponds to a low-dimensional manifold in activation space and proposes projecting steering interventions onto that manifold to cut output tokens by up to 71% without hurting accuracy.
sources.title: Mitigating Overthinking in Large Reasoning Models via Manifold Steering

instructions:
Revise the wiki definition for 'Manifold Steering'.

It was written against fewer sources than the archive now holds. The sources below are all of them, including the ones that have arrived since.

This is the definition as it stands:

    An overthinking-mitigation technique that identifies overthinking as movement along a low-dimensional manifold in a reasoning model's activation space, then steers activations along that manifold at inference time to shorten reasoning. Its source paper reports cutting output tokens up to 71% while maintaining or improving accuracy; the 'Don't Overthink It' survey categorizes it under 'Representation Engineering', alongside similar steering-vector methods (SEAL, Pre-allocated Direction Vectors, Thinking Progress Vector).

**Keep what still holds.** Change it where a later source contradicts it, narrows it, or shows the term being used in a way the old text does not cover — and say so plainly rather than hedging the original into something vaguer. If the new sources change nothing, return it unchanged; that is a real answer and it records that somebody checked.

A definition that enumerates its sources by name is the one most likely to be quietly wrong now. Prefer stating what the term means to counting where it appears.

result.definition: A training-free, inference-time steering method that treats overthinking in a reasoning model as movement along a low-dimensional manifold of its residual-stream activations, recovered via PCA. It extracts an 'overthinking direction' by difference-in-means between overthinking and non-overthinking activations, projects that direction onto the PCA manifold, and ablates the projected component at inference time -- a step motivated by the finding that ablating the raw, unprojected difference-in-means direction only reduces overthinking up to a point, after which its effect plateaus and then reverses as intervention strength increases, corrupting other model abilities. The source paper reports this projection removes that accuracy-degrading interference noise and cuts output tokens by up to 71% while maintaining or improving accuracy. The 'Don't Overthink It' survey classifies it under 'Representation Engineering', alongside other steering-vector methods (SEAL, Pre-allocated Direction Vectors, Thinking Progress Vector).
